A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoCA. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support reliable comparison and identification of relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes experiments covering planning, cross-city adaptation, active learning, image degradations, and loss ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original nuScenes results and adds simulation, cross-domain, ablation, agent-prediction, and training-diagnostic results.

M1.justification: The codebook, GP architecture, and staged training procedure remain. However, the stated losses change: negative log-sigma terms become positive, and the negative agent-motion term in v1 Eq. 5 becomes positive in v3 Eq. 6. These are limited objective corrections; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes or reruns.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates nuScenes, including city transfer, turning and long-tail scenarios, low light, and motion blur. v3 adds Bench2Drive, Bench2Drive-to-nuScenes transfer, NAVSIM v1, and DriveArena evaluations, substantially extending environmental and interactive-driving coverage. Snow and fog are also added.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparators including SSR, ORION, GenAD, and DriveTransformer in new experiments. Senna and DiMA join the retained cross-city and long-tail comparisons. Active learning gains MC Dropout and Deep Ensemble comparisons, while Table 14 compares GP planning against MLP, diffusion, and VAE heads.

E3.justification: New protocols include Bench2Drive training on 1,000 clips and evaluation on 220 routes, closed-loop driving and ability metrics, and 12-epoch source training followed by 12-epoch sim-to-real adaptation. NAVSIM and DriveArena introduce additional planning metrics. Corruption experiments now include supervised and unsupervised adaptation, and agent prediction adds minADE/minFDE. The original nuScenes protocol is retained.

E4.justification: The original loss ablation is retained as Table 11. New analyses test kernel choice, trajectory-codebook diversity, alternative planner heads, and stronger uncertainty-based sampling methods. Appendix H adds variance and embedding evolution during training and uncertainty comparisons across ordinary and long-tail scenes. Corruption robustness also gains adaptation analyses.

E5.justification: v3 first reports numerical GP predictive variances across scene categories and a variance-versus-training curve in Table 19 and Figure 5; v1 describes and uses this uncertainty without reporting those diagnostics. This expands model-uncertainty reporting, not uncertainty around benchmark performance: neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial closed-loop, transfer, robustness, and ablation results. New Table 18 reports agent minADE/minFDE of 0.62/0.99 for SparseDrive-S versus 0.54/0.83 with RoCA regularization. Many original nuScenes results remain unchanged. Some retained cross-city entries change beyond rounding: VAD-Tiny unsupervised Singapore-to-Boston L2 changes from 0.951 in v1 Table 2 to 0.94 in v3 Table 3, without an explained setting change.

T1.justification: The loss-sign corrections revise the mathematical content of the claimed Gaussian-likelihood objectives, rather than merely changing notation. The predictive-variance expression is also corrected. v3 adds standard GP background in Section 3.1 and Appendix C, but no new theorem, proof, or substantive theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The central claims about GP-based generalization, adaptation, and uncertainty-guided active learning remain essentially unchanged. The contribution list explicitly extends the stated scope to closed-loop evaluation and simulation-to-real transfer. The conclusion drops v1's explicit nuScenes state-of-the-art claim while retaining the broader robustness claims.

C2.justification: v3 elaborates the existing mechanism explanation through comparisons with deterministic anchors, semantic interpretations of token subclusters, and higher long-tail variance interpreted as lower confidence. It also interprets the new kernel and codebook ablations. These refine the original explanation rather than replace it; substantial new limitations or failure-boundary discussion is absent.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the 256-dimensional basis tokens, adds Algorithm 2 documenting the existing unsupervised-adaptation procedure, and supplies budgets for the new transfer experiments. Original nuScenes hardware, staged training durations, and computational-cost measurements are retained. The additions remain limited, and Algorithm 2 inconsistently mentions standard trajectory losses despite its unsupervised setting.

R1.justification: v3 substantially broadens the comparison landscape through newer driving models, simulation benchmarks, uncertainty-estimation approaches, and additional GP vision literature. Appendix B explicitly positions GP planning against alternative planner heads, while the active-learning discussion compares uncertainty approaches. Several earlier multitask-driving references disappear, although the central positioning of GP integration into autonomous driving remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: closed-loop and transfer experiments lead the evaluation, standardized nuScenes evaluation moves into Appendix A, and earlier training, computation, and ablation appendices become its subsections. Related work is condensed, the problem formulation gains GP preliminaries, and several experimental explanations and the conclusion are rewritten.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column presentation. Figure 1 gains explicit loss and supervision annotations; the t-SNE display is revised to annotated city panels and enlarged in the appendix. Numerous new tables, expanded comparator and corruption tables, and training-diagnostic plots substantially change the visual presentation. Existing qualitative examples are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important weakness of v1's deployment claims: reliance on open-loop nuScenes evidence. Closed-loop and cross-domain evaluations, stronger active-learning comparators, and targeted kernel, codebook, and planner-head ablations substantially strengthen empirical support. Corrected loss signs improve mathematical consistency. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including unexplained cross-city numerical changes and inconsistent unsupervised-adaptation pseudocode; benchmark uncertainty reporting remains limited.
